query: In Werkzeug, when a file or a path is served back to the client as a WSGI response, how are the download name and content type worked out, which headers are produced for downloading, caching and conditional or range requests, and which invalid inputs cause errors?

operations.name: A text-mode file object is rejected
expressions: raise ValueError("File must be in binary mode, or 'BytesIO'.")

operations.name: A non-ASCII download name produces both a plain and an RFC 5987 encoded filename
An attachment without any name is rejected
expressions: "No name provided for attachment. Either pass 'download_name', or"

operations.name: X-Sendfile mode hands the path to the server and empties the body
Conditional and range handling is applied, and the response is closed if it fails

dependencies.name: A content encoding header is only sent when the file is not an attachment
expressions: if encoding is not None and not as_attachment:

dependencies.name: For a path the size and modification time come from stat; for a file object they come from seeking, falling back to its file descriptor
Responses default to no-cache; a positive max age makes them public and sets an expiry
An ETag given as a string is used as is; otherwise it is built from modification time and size
